'''''Numbers: The Universal Language''''' ({{langx|fr|'''L'empire des nombres'''|translation=The Empire of Numbers}}) is a 1996 [[Livre d'art|illustrated]] [[monograph]] on [[number]]s and [[Number#History|their history]]. Written by the French historian of science [[Denis Guedj]], and published in [[Pocket edition|pocket format]] by [[Éditions Gallimard]] as the {{ordinal|300}} volume in their "[[Découvertes Gallimard|Découvertes]]" collection<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gallimard.fr/Catalogue/GALLIMARD/Decouvertes-Gallimard/Decouvertes-Gallimard/Sciences-et-techniques/L-empire-des-nombres |title=L'empire des nombres, Collection Découvertes Gallimard (n° 300), Série Sciences et techniques |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated--> |website=gallimard.fr |language=fr |access-date=7 December 2020}}</ref> (known as "Abrams Discoveries" in the United States, and "New Horizons" in the United Kingdom). The book was adapted into a documentary film of the same title in 2001.<ref name="arte">{{cite web |url=http://download.pro.arte.tv/archives/fichiers/01678492.pdf |title=L'Aventure humaine — L'empire des nombres |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2001 |website=pro.arte.tv |language=fr |access-date=29 November 2020}}</ref>

== Introduction ==
[[File:Numbers - The Universal Language ("Abrams Discoveries" and "New Horizons").jpg|thumb|left|240px|From left: US and UK editions. The covers featuring the ten digits interpreted by the computer artist Julio Bravo, 1997.]]
The book is part of the {{lang|fr|Sciences et techniques}} series (formerly belonging to {{lang|fr|Sciences}} series) in the "[[Découvertes Gallimard]]" collection. As a work of popularisation of [[mathematics]], it uses simple language to describe the basics of numbers—[[arithmetic]], [[integer]], [[natural number]], concepts of [[0|zero]] and [[infinity]]—as well as how numbers and their symbolism came to be used in art and other disciplines.

According to the tradition of "Découvertes", which is based on an abundant pictorial documentation and a way of bringing together visual documents and texts, enhanced by printing on coated paper, as commented in ''[[L'Express]]'', "genuine monographs, published like [[Livre d'art|art books]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lexpress.fr/culture/livre/l-invention-des-decouvertes_810690.html |title=L'invention des Découvertes |last=Garcia |first=Daniel |date=1 November 2005 |website=[[L'Express|lexpress.fr]] |language=fr |access-date=29 November 2020 |quote=De véritables monographies, éditées comme des livres d'art.}}</ref> It's almost like a "[[graphic novel]]", replete with colour plates.

== Contents ==
The book opens with a "trailer" ({{pp.|1|9}}), that is, a series of full-page photographs showing ''The [[Power of 10|Powers of Ten]]''. The body text is divided into seven chapters:
{{div col|colwidth=25em}}
* Chapter 1: "How Many?" ({{pp.|13|23}});
* Chapter 2: "From Numbers to Figures" ({{pp.|25|43}});
* Chapter 3: "Positional Notation" ({{pp.|45|59}});
* Chapter 4: "Natural Numbers" ({{pp.|61|77}});
* Chapter 5: "The Universe Expands" ({{pp.|79|103}});
* Chapter 6: "From Zero to Infinity" ({{pp.|105|121}});
* Chapter 7: "The Impossible Definition" ({{pp.|123|127}}).
{{div col end}}

The second part of the book, the "Documents", containing a compilation of excerpts divided into nine parts:
{{div col|colwidth=25em}}
# Counting ({{pp.|130|131}});
# Against Pythagoras, Against Zeno ({{pp.|132|135}});
# Numbers and religion ({{pp.|136|137}});
# Numbers, philosophy, and poetry ({{pp.|138|141}});
# The science of measurement ({{pp.|142|145}});
# The abacus and calculator ({{pp.|146|147}});
# Music and mathematics ({{pp.|148|151}});
# Number and psychology ({{pp.|152|155}});
# The wit and wisdom of numbers ({{pp.|156|163}}).
* Amusing Puzzle ({{p.|164}});
* Glossary ({{pp.|165|167}});
* Chronology ({{pp.|168|170}});
* Further Reading ({{p.|170}});
* List of Illustrations ({{pp.|171|173}});
* Index ({{pp.|173|174}}).
{{div col end}}

== Reception ==
On [[Babelio]], the book gets an average of 3.0/5 based on 11 ratings.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.babelio.com/livres/Guedj-LEmpire-des-nombres/3153 |title=L'Empire des nombres |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=babelio.com |language=fr |access-date=29 November 2020}}</ref> [[Goodreads]] reported, based on 66 ratings, an average of 3.61 out of 5,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/1232290 |title=Numbers: The Universal Language |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=goodreads.com |access-date=29 November 2020}}</ref> indicating "generally positive opinions".

== Adaptation ==
In 2001, the book was adapted as a documentary film of the same name. A co-production between La Sept-Arte and Trans Europe Film, with the collaboration of Éditions Gallimard and [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] Images Média, the film was directed by [[Philippe Truffault]], with [[voice-over]] narration by [[Denis Guedj]] himself. It was broadcast on [[Arte]] as part of the television programme ''[[The Human Adventure (TV series)|The Human Adventure]]'',<ref name="arte" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.florilege-maths.fr/fiche/lempire-des-nombres-2/ |title=L'empire des nombres 2001 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2001 |website=florilege-maths.fr |language=fr |access-date=29 November 2020}}</ref> and released on DVD by Arte vidéo, with English dubbed audio.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.amazon.com/Denis-Guedj/dp/B001E9FDW6 |title=L'Empire des Nombres (DVD) |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated--> |website=amazon.com |access-date=29 November 2020}}</ref> The film has also been dubbed into German by the title {{lang|de|Im Reich der Zahlen}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://programm.ard.de/TV/arte/im-reich-der-zahlen/eid_287247507269402 |title=Im Reich der Zahlen |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=10 March 2012 |website=programm.ard.de |language=de |access-date=29 November 2020}}</ref>
